answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers attest fraud. Like a river that only flows where the channel is dug, trust builds only through verified work over time. Forging many identities gets expensive because each fake must forge its own bond and history, while a lagoon of idle, unbonded accounts earns nothing and cannot flood the market.
